markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable change: add recency-weighted historical evidence to SASRec and measure whether it improves the pinned macro validation HR@10. The supplied feedback motivates this hypothesis; it does not establish measured model defects.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Feedback favors recent, repeated interests. Existing margin probes cannot measure reliance on those interests. (2) Directional embedding similarity does not establish ranking quality. Empty probe observations must indicate unavailable evidence. (3) Compatibility and unmet need appear in feedback. Histories alone establish neither ownership nor requirements, and missing descriptions prevent reliable compatibility judgments.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows sampled metrics can change model ordering. Preserve the host’s candidate protocol for selection. (2) [Robust Training](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) motivates controlled history removals. Sensitivity demonstrates model dependence, not causal preferences. (3) [Spotify’s study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) motivates simple historical evidence models. Its results do not establish transfer to these Amazon datasets.

These insights define three directions: historical evidence aggregation, controlled behavioral diagnostics, and text-grounded assessability. A common framework maps **evidence → intervention → measurement**: histories → recency residual → pinned HR@10; history removals → matched perturbations → target-rank changes; descriptions → supported attribute extraction → coverage and explicit conflicts. The gap is connecting diagnostic signals to independently measured predictive gains.

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, with difficulty increasing with implementation effort:

- **Recency residual: 4/7/3.** Originality: useful combination, but familiar components. Potential: cheap cross-category hypothesis, but recent events may be incidental. Difficulty: one scoring branch, but predictor parity needs care. Reference: Spotify study.
- **Matched removal probe: 5/7/4.** Originality: feedback-specific controls, but established perturbation methods. Potential: tests evidence dependence, but gives no causal interpretation. Difficulty: reusable scoring hooks, but padding controls matter. Reference: Robust Training.
- **Attribute-conflict probe: 5/6/7.** Originality: connects assessability with failures, but extraction is established. Potential: distinguishes unknown from conflict, but text may be sparse. Difficulty: deterministic rules are feasible, but normalization requires auditing. Reference: [WDC-PAVE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02130).

Select the **recency residual**. Pool valid historical item embeddings with exponential age weights, then add their candidate dot product to SASRec’s score through a learned nonnegative scalar per dataset. Repeated items contribute repeatedly; no semantic compatibility is inferred. Train with the baseline loss and seeds, comparing against the unchanged baseline within the shared budget.

Pseudocode: `weights = normalize(exp(-log(2)*age/4)); pool = sum(weights*emb(history)); score = sasrec_score + sigmoid(a_dataset)*dot(pool, emb(candidate))`.

Use causal prefix pools during training and full observed histories during inference. Update the predictor writer and compatibility scoring hook together. Retain required diagnostic APIs; report observation counts and matched-removal effects as exploratory evidence. Select solely by the four-category macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Add a learned recency-weighted item-embedding residual to each dataset’s SASRec scorer. Preserve all four independently routed models and select using the pinned macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests that broad historical affinity sometimes outranks specific recent or repeated interests. A small historical-evidence branch directly tests this hypothesis without requiring unavailable ratings, reviews, ownership labels, simulator traits, or pretrained weights.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, unchanged splits, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Respect the environment’s SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200 and single-GPU execution. Start with a fixed four-interaction half-life, explicitly a hypothesis rather than an established optimum. Learn one sigmoid-constrained residual weight per dataset, initialized to 0.1. At each valid training position pool only the visible causal prefix, using cumulative exponentially weighted sums to avoid quadratic work; exclude padding and targets. Use the same item embeddings and baseline training loss. Compare the unchanged baseline with this single modification, charging all runs to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Apply the residual consistently in training, validation, the compatibility view’s predict_score, and generated working/predict.py; save the gate and pooling configuration with checkpoints. Keep view.model as the actual nn.Module. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics plus definitions and observation counts; unavailable measurements must be null or explicitly unavailable. Replace unavailable metadata category breakdowns with routing-dataset and training-frequency summaries. Use training-derived chronological holdouts for matched recent-versus-random removal diagnostics, separate from host selection. Do not infer ownership, satisfaction, compatibility, or latent traits from interactions. No performance improvement has been measured.
idea.pseudocode:
For each routed dataset:
  initialize baseline SASRec and scalar a = logit(0.1)
  for each baseline training batch:
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    pool = causal_exponential_pool(item_emb(sequence), half_life=4, ignore_padding=True)
    score(features, pool, items) = baseline_score(features, items) + sigmoid(a) * dot(pool, item_emb(items))
    optimize baseline loss using modified positive and negative scores
  save architecture configuration, model state, and gate beneath trial directory
Generate predictor with identical pooling, scoring, and dataset routing.
Compare baseline and modified models using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
Run matched-removal diagnostics separately; interpret only measured metrics with definitions and counts.

originality.positive: Combines explicit historical evidence with a sequence model in a minimal form tied to the supplied diagnostic hypothesis.
originality.negative: Recency pooling, residual scoring, and learned mixture weights are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides a cheap foundation for studying when recent historical evidence improves sequential ranking across datasets.
future_potential.negative: Potential gains may depend on category-specific purchasing cycles and the benchmark’s sampled candidates.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires one causal pooling operation, one scalar parameter per routed model, and a scoring addition.
code_difficulty.negative: Training-prefix alignment, padding, checkpoint loading, and predictor compatibility must remain consistent.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes that sampled evaluation can change model orderings, motivating strict preservation of the pinned selection protocol.
limitations: Does not establish which architecture will improve this benchmark or equate sampled HR@10 with full-catalog quality.

related_work.title: Robust Training of Sequential Recommender Systems with Missing Input Data
contributions: Studies ranking sensitivity to missing historical interactions and motivates controlled removal diagnostics.
limitations: Perturbation sensitivity does not identify causal user preferences or prove transfer to the requested datasets.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: Reports strong history-aware pairwise baselines, motivating a simple historical-evidence branch.
limitations: The supplied results concern other benchmarks and do not validate this specific residual architecture.

related_work.title: WDC-PAVE
contributions: Provides precedent for extracting and normalizing product attributes with verified annotations.
limitations: Extraction needs auditing on available titles and descriptions; missing attributes cannot establish compatibility or conflict.
